question: What causes the yellowish skin color seen in neonatal jaundice?

options.A: An excess of white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: A temporary infection of the newborn's liver
options.C: Low levels of iron stored in newborn tissues
options.D: The accumulation of bilirubin in the body

explanation: Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced when red blood cells break down, and it builds up in the skin and eyes when the baby's body cannot clear it fast enough. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which body part usually shows the yellow discoloration first when a baby develops jaundice?
explanation: Jaundice typically starts from the head and moves downward, meaning the eyes and face show the yellow color before the trunk and limbs do. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which enzyme in the liver changes unconjugated bilirubin into a water-soluble form?
explanation: Glucuronyl transferase is the key liver enzyme responsible for conjugating bilirubin so the body can excrete it safely. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: Why is unconjugated bilirubin dangerous to a newborn's brain?

options.A: It triggers an immediate allergic reaction inside brain cells
options.B: It dissolves easily in body fats and can cross the blood-brain barrier
options.C: It blocks blood vessels supplying the brainstem directly
options.D: It binds permanently to red blood cells and deprives the brain of oxygen

explanation: Because unconjugated bilirubin is fat-soluble, it can easily slip across the immature blood-brain barrier in a newborn. Understanding this helps you see why keeping track of bilirubin levels is so vital! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: What is a key sign that a baby has pathological jaundice instead of normal physiological jaundice?

options.A: The baby feeding well and crying with a strong voice
options.B: Yellow skin fading completely by the end of the second week
options.C: Yellow color appearing within the first 24 hours of life
options.D: Jaundice showing up strictly on the third day after birth

explanation: Normal physiological jaundice takes a little time to show up. Any yellow color appearing on day one (within 24 hours) is a red flag that needs a closer look by the medical team. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: A healthy term baby develops mild yellow skin on day three of life, which gradually disappears by day ten without treatment. How is this classified?
explanation: Jaundice that appears after 24 hours, peaks early, and resolves on its own within two weeks in a healthy infant is normal physiological jaundice. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: Which inherited enzyme deficiency is a major risk factor for severe neonatal jaundice in Nigeria?
explanation: G6PD deficiency is prevalent in the region and makes newborn red cells very fragile when exposed to certain oxidative triggers like camphor. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: A mother brings her 3-day-old baby to the clinic with severe jaundice and mentions storing baby clothes with traditional camphor. What likely caused this?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the scent of the fabric softener used
options.B: Blockage of the newborn bile ducts caused by dust inhalation
options.C: Direct contamination of the skin by toxic chemicals in the air
options.D: Oxidative destruction of red blood cells in a baby with an enzyme defect

explanation: Camphor fumes from stored clothes can trigger rapid breakdown of red blood cells (hemolysis) in babies with G6PD deficiency. This is a very important health education point for mothers in Nigeria! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: How can a nurse best check a baby's skin for a yellow tint during a physical exam?

options.A: Gently pressing the skin over a bony prominence to blanch it
options.B: Pinching a fold of skin on the baby's arm to test elasticity
options.C: Observing the baby inside a dark room using a standard flashlight
options.D: Shining a blue phototherapy light directly onto the infant's abdomen

explanation: Pressing gently over a bone clears the surface blood for a second, making the underlying yellow bilirubin tint much easier to spot. Simple and effective bedside nursing! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: Which finding in a jaundiced newborn must be reported immediately because it points to bile duct disease?

options.C: Yellow skin extending to the toes

explanation: Stools that look pale or clay-colored mean bile isn't reaching the gut, which can signal a serious condition like biliary atresia. You are learning to spot the critical details! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: What is the best test to confirm the exact bilirubin level in a newborn?
explanation: While skin scanners are quick, a blood test gives the exact measurement the doctor needs to decide if phototherapy is necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: Why are transcutaneous (skin) bilirubin readings often followed up with a blood test when numbers are high?

options.A: Skin devices can be influenced by skin tone and are only meant for screening
options.B: Transcutaneous meters measure direct bilirubin instead of total bilirubin
options.C: Skin readings only work accurately after the baby is two weeks old
options.D: Blood tests are required by law before a baby can start breastfeeding

explanation: Handheld skin scanners are wonderful for quick checks, but a blood test gives us the exact numbers needed for treatment decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: How does standard phototherapy help lower bilirubin levels in a newborn?

options.A: It cools down the infant's skin to slow down the circulation of blood
options.B: It destroys red blood cells so they stop producing extra waste pigments
options.C: It stimulates the kidneys to produce concentrated, dark-colored urine
options.D: It changes bilirubin into water-soluble forms that the body can excrete easily

explanation: Special lights alter the bilirubin right in the skin, turning it into a form the baby can easily pass out without needing the liver to process it first. Science in action! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: When is an exchange transfusion chosen over standard phototherapy?

options.A: When bilirubin levels are critically high and threatening the brain
options.B: When the baby develops a mild diaper rash during light treatment
options.C: When the baby has mild jaundice lasting longer than two weeks
options.D: When the mother wants to formula feed instead of breastfeeding

explanation: An exchange transfusion is an emergency procedure used when bilirubin levels are dangerously high, quickly swapping the baby's blood to protect their brain. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: What is the term for permanent brain damage caused by untreated severe neonatal jaundice?
explanation: Kernicterus is the permanent neurological condition that happens when high levels of bilirubin damage the brain. This is why our nursing care and monitoring are so important! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h8)

question: Which clinical sign is a classic indicator of acute bilirubin entering the brain in a newborn?

options.A: Having an abnormally fast breathing rate with chest indrawing
options.B: Passing frequent watery green stools during feeding times
options.C: Developing a sudden red rash across the chest and abdomen
options.D: Arching the back and neck backward into an opisthotonos position

explanation: Opisthotonos (severe backward arching of the body) is a classic warning sign that bilirubin is irritating the baby's central nervous system. You're building expert clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h8)

question: What is a mandatory safety action when a newborn is receiving phototherapy?

options.A: Keeping the incubator lights turned off at all times
options.B: Covering the infant's eyes with protective patches
options.C: Applying heavy moisturizing lotion to the skin every hour
options.D: Wrapping the baby tightly in warm blankets to prevent chills

explanation: Always make sure the baby's eyes are securely covered with eye patches to protect their delicate retina from the bright phototherapy lights. Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h9)

question: Why must nurses encourage frequent feeding for a newborn undergoing treatment for jaundice?

options.A: Sucking on the breast helps strengthen the neck muscles against stiffness
options.B: Feeding provides extra calories to help the liver produce more red blood cells
options.C: Milk intake cools the digestive tract and prevents stomach irritation from lights
options.D: Regular feeds promote bowel movements, which help clear bilirubin out of the body

explanation: Frequent feeds mean regular bowel movements, and that is the main way the baby's body passes out the broken-down bilirubin. Feedings are treatment too! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h9)
